scenes.say: Your AI agent just refunded a customer. Twice.
scenes.cap: Your AI agent just refunded a customer. Twice.

scenes.say: Here's what happened. The agent was on step two, the refund, when its server was shut down. The bank paid out, but the agent never heard back. So when it restarted, it remembered nothing, and did it all again.
scenes.cap: Here's what happened. The agent was on step two, the refund, when its server was shut down. The bank paid out, but the agent never heard back. So when it restarted, it remembered nothing, and did it all again.

scenes.say: This isn't a new problem. Databases have faced it for fifty years. After a crash, how do you know what you already did?
scenes.cap: This isn't a new problem. Databases have faced it for 50 years. After a crash, how do you know what you already did?

scenes.say: The obvious fix is to save the whole file on every change. But if the power fails halfway through that save, the old data is already gone, and the new data is only half written.
scenes.cap: The obvious fix is to save the whole file on every change. But if the power fails halfway through that save, the old data is already gone, and the new data is only half written.

scenes.say: We tested every possible crash moment. Six hundred and thirty-four, out of six hundred and sixty-four, lose data the user was told was saved.
scenes.cap: We tested every possible crash moment. 634 out of 664 lose data the user was told was saved.

scenes.say: The real fix is almost too simple. Never overwrite. Before you change anything, append a short note to the end of a log. If the power fails, only the very last note can tear, and that one was never confirmed anyway. Zero out of two hundred and thirty crash points lose saved data.
scenes.cap: The real fix is almost too simple. Never overwrite. Before you change anything, append a short note to the end of a log. If the power fails, only the very last note can tear, and that one was never confirmed anyway. 0 out of 230 crash points lose saved data.

scenes.say: One catch. When a program writes to a file, the data sits in memory for a while. It's only safe once a call named eff-sync confirms it reached the disk. Say saved only after that.
scenes.cap: One catch. When a program writes to a file, the data sits in memory for a while. It's only safe once a call named fsync confirms it reached the disk. Say “saved” only after that.

scenes.say: Now give the agent the same log. Before each step, write down what you're about to do. After it, write down the result. On restart, skip what's done, and retry the unfinished step with the same idempotency key. The payment system replies: already done. One refund.
scenes.cap: Now give the agent the same log. Before each step, write down what you're about to do. After it, write down the result. On restart, skip what's done, and retry the unfinished step with the same idempotency key. The payment system replies: already done. One refund.

scenes.say: That's a write-ahead log. Append, never overwrite. Saved means eff-sync returned. And for agents, journal the results. The log is the truth.
scenes.cap: That's a write-ahead log. Append, never overwrite. Saved means fsync returned. And for agents, journal the results. The log is the truth.
